title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: ASEAN heads of state adopted the ASEAN Declaration on the Placement and Protection of Migrant Fishers and the ASEAN Declaration on the Protection of Migrant Workers and Family Members in Crisis Situations in 2023. The former calls for actions to address abuse & exploitation against migrant fishers, including strengthening labour inspection & referral systems. The latter calls for inclusion of migrant workers and their families in crisis preparedness, response and recovery frameworks in ASEAN and timely access to safety, health care and support services, acknowledges the need to provide humanitarian assistance to all migrant resident in the country irrespective of their legal status. Guidelines to support implementation of this Declaration referring to ILS were adopted in 2023. At the 15th ASEAN Forum on Migrant Labour (AFML) in 2022, members adopted recommendations ensuring that resumption of labour migration in ASEAN is rights-responsive and maximizes development impacts on migrant workers. At the 16th AFML in 2023, members adopted recommendations towards enhancing legal pathways for labour migration and streamlining/simplifying regular migration channels. This included recommendations on making labour migration programmes more gender responsive, safe, affordable, accessible and efficient. In November 2022, ASEAN sectoral bodies and senior officials from ASEAN Member States adopted recommendations on strengthening regional information-sharing, cross border cooperation and establishing referral mechanisms on the prevention and investigation of Trafficking In Persons and Forced Labour. South Asian Member States developed a South Asian Qualification Referencing Framework (SAQRF) to enhance the transparency and recognition of qualifications, promote the mobility of learners and workers and provide a link to other regional qualification frameworks. ILO inputs to the ASEAN Declaration and Guidelines on the Protection of Migrant Workers and Family Members in Crisis Situations, with the support of the governments of Australia and Canada, included a background paper, comments on the zero draft declaration, drafting the zero draft Guidelines, and supporting one online tripartite plus consultation and one in-person consultation. ILO inputs to the ASEAN Declaration on the Placement and Protection of Migrant Fishers, with the support of the EU, included comments on the zero draft declaration and supporting a tripartite plus consultation. ILO inputs to the 15th and 16th AFMLs, with the support of the Governments of Australia and Canada, included thematic background papers, a progress review, tripartite plus national preparatory meetings, regional preparatory meetings for employers and workers, technical inputs and support to the hosts. ILO inputs, with the support of the Governments of Australia and Canada, to the ASEAN Guidelines on portability of social security benefits include technical support from migration and social protection experts, drafting the zero draft guidelines, and supporting the first consultation. With support from EU, ILO provided support to Lao PDR in hosting the ASEAN workshop on strengthening coordination on the prevention and investigation of Trafficking in Persons and Forced Labour. In such regional events, ILO’s standards provide a baseline in the drafting of recommendations. With support from the Government of Switzerland, ILO supported the development of the SAQRF through the drafting of a background report and concept proposal, the convening of four virtual consultations, and the organization of an in-person experts meeting.
